claims.claim: She revs the engine only in the last hundred pages, after ensconcing the reader, which multiplies payoff and heartbreak.
claims.source: Ilana Teitelbaum, Los Angeles Review of Books (2014)
claims.quote: revving the engine in the hundred pages before the end

claims.claim: The important thing between characters is what is not said.
claims.source: Ilana Teitelbaum, Los Angeles Review of Books (2014)
claims.quote: what is most important is what is not said

claims.claim: There is no magic moment of overcoming; childhood traumas linger and take new shapes as Fitz ages.
claims.source: Ilana Teitelbaum, Los Angeles Review of Books (2014)
claims.quote: no magic moment of overcoming the past

claims.claim: Magic and brutal violence are fuel for the psychological dimension, not the other way around.
claims.source: Ilana Teitelbaum, Los Angeles Review of Books (2014)

claims.claim: The early Farseer volumes are couched as a painfully confessional memoir presented as a manuscript for future perusal.
Langford finds the reader feels every blow, sword-cut and fever.
claims.quote: You feel every blow, sword-cut and fever suffered

claims.claim: How Fitz reacts to things is the story; four-fifths of a book can be tea and clothes and remain the best part.
claims.source: Vacuous Wastrel review of Fool's Assassin (2014)
claims.quote: how Fitz reacts to things is the story

claims.claim: Even when Fitz is calm and happy the prose shows him working hard to stay so.
claims.source: Vacuous Wastrel review of Fool's Assassin (2014)
claims.quote: even when Fitz is calm and happy

claims.claim: Fitz's prose feels natural because it is intimate, but its clarity is literary intelligence, not simplicity.
claims.source: The Huntress and the Wolf (Substack essay)
claims.quote: intimacy should not be mistaken for simplicity

claims.claim: Fitz narrates his doubts, failures, grief and shame while his competence passes without comment.
claims.source: The Huntress and the Wolf (Substack essay)
claims.quote: his doubts, failures, grief, and shame

claims.claim: Character is shown through inventories of the mundane on the mantel and the desk.
claims.source: The Huntress and the Wolf (Substack essay)
claims.quote: medicinal unguents on the mantel, two pens at the ready

claims.claim: Characters are so real that readers stay fascinated even while they perform the most routine tasks.
claims.quote: even when they are performing the most routine tasks

claims.claim: A sympathetic critic finds overreliance on adverbs stunts the Liveship novels' flow.
claims.quote: overreliance on adverbs often stunts the novel's flow

claims.feature: loss as what is not received
claims.claim: Loss is rendered through what Fitz does not get, and compressed with 'After a time'.
claims.source: Jeffrey David Outcalt, Substack close reading
claims.quote: no princess saved, no true love

claims.claim: She never shies from the exhausting reality of traveling, hunting and dealing with other people.
claims.quote: the exhausting reality of traveling, hunting, dealing with other people

verdicts.trueWording: revving the engine in the hundred pages before the end
verdicts.note: LARB (Teitelbaum, 8 Sep 2014) verbatim; continues "By doing so only after she has taken care to ensconce the reader ... she increases the payoff (and the heartbreak) at the end exponentially" - every limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: what is most important is what is not said
verdicts.note: Verbatim on the LARB page, applied to "much of the character development in the series" and illustrated by the Chade/Fitz exchange, so the "between characters" limb holds.

verdicts.trueWording: no magic moment of overcoming the past
verdicts.note: Verbatim, and the sentence continues "the traumas of childhood abandonment and abuse linger and take new shapes as Fitz matures to adulthood" - both limbs supported word for word.

verdicts.trueWording: magic and brutal violence are fuel for the psychological dimension, not the other way around
verdicts.note: Verbatim on the LARB page including the "not the other way around" clause.

verdicts.trueWording: couched in the form of a painfully confessional memoir written and presented as a manuscript for future perusal
verdicts.note: SFE entry "Hobb, Robin" (updated 6 Oct 2025), signed [JC] = John Clute, so the attribution holds; scoped to "especially in the first volumes", matching the claim's "early Farseer volumes".

verdicts.trueWording: You feel every blow, sword-cut and fever suffered by the hapless Fitz
verdicts.note: Ansible 1997 SFX Reviews, stated header: "reviews written by David Langford for SFX magazine in 1997". The #assassin section is Assassin's Quest (SFX #24, April 1997).

verdicts.trueWording: How Fitz reacts to things is the story, is the point of the things that go on around him
verdicts.note: Quote verbatim (only a sentence-initial capital differs). Second limb supported on the same page: the review opens with the "4/5ths of the book was pointless filler" charge it rejects, and later says "The bulk of this book is probably my favourite and almost certainly the best of Hobb's novels", alongside "I'd be quite happy just reading three books of the man sitting around, hanging out, having tea with people, deciding which clothes to buy".

verdicts.trueWording: even when Fitz is calm and happy, he is having to work hard at being calm and happy
verdicts.note: Verbatim; the page frames it as "There is a strong feeling that ...", which supports the claim's "the prose shows him working hard to stay so".

verdicts.trueWording: His prose feels natural because it is intimate, but intimacy should not be mistaken for simplicity
verdicts.note: Verbatim, and the next sentence supplies the second limb: "The clarity with which he renders character, politics, landscape, memory, and moral conflict is itself evidence of extraordinary literary intelligence."

verdicts.trueWording: He narrates his doubts, failures, grief, and shame
verdicts.note: Verbatim, and the asymmetry limb is the next sentence: "The moments where he is operating at full capacity pass without comment because, to him, they are simply what he does."

verdicts.trueWording: cataloged the medicinal unguents on the mantel, the two pens at the ready
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: the desk - the page names no desk anywhere (grep for "desk" returns zero hits); the catalogue is the mantel, the two pens, and "the Stones puzzle on the table"
verdicts.note: Also note the supplied quote is not word-for-word: the page reads "the two pens at the ready" (definite article dropped in the claim). The mantel/inventory-as-characterisation core is supported - Fitz cataloguing Lant's room as evidence of training that "is still running beneath the surface constantly and automatically".

verdicts.trueWording: her characters are so real and so engaging that you can't help but to be fascinated by them, even when they are performing the most routine tasks
verdicts.note: Verbatim on the Hippogriff's Aerie Fool's Assassin review; the page continues "or having pages of conversations".

verdicts.trueWording: Her overreliance on adverbs often stunts the novel's flow
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: the plural "the Liveship novels'" - the page says "the novel's flow" (singular), inside its Ship of Magic discussion; it makes no such charge against The Mad Ship or Ship of Destiny
verdicts.note: Quotation verbatim. "Sympathetic critic" is supported: the piece (Lew Kelly, Fantasy-Faction, 19 Aug 2014) opens "Credit goes to Robin Hobb for doing something new and challenging" and calls the trilogy "wonderfully plotted with plenty of deeply created characters".

verdicts.trueWording: There is no princess saved, no true love. The hero is not lauded by the realm and given riches
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: compressed with 'After a time' - the essay never discusses that phrase as a device; "After a time" occurs exactly once on the page, inside a block quotation of Hobb's novel (Starling's kiss), with no analytic comment on it
verdicts.note: The loss-as-absence limb is supported verbatim. Jeffrey O, "Lies Are What A Man Needs Most", 20 Jan 2025.

verdicts.trueWording: Hobb never shies away from the exhausting reality of traveling, hunting, dealing with other people
verdicts.note: Verbatim (page continues "-- and dealing with dragons"). Molly Templeton, Reactor, published 7 June 2019, originally May 2017; the sentence sits in the Rain Wild Chronicles section but is phrased as a general statement about Hobb.
